name: immunoglobulin lambda locus

function.text: IGL is the immunoglobulin lambda light-chain locus and contributes to antibody diversity through variable-to-joining segment rearrangement in B cells.

function.text: IGL is the immunoglobulin lambda light-chain locus. In developing B cells, a variable segment joins a joining segment at the DNA level, and the constant segment is incorporated by RNA splicing. Use of different segments, junctional diversity, and somatic hypermutation contribute to antibody diversity. The locus contains both functional segments and pseudogenes, so its organization differs from that of a conventional single protein-coding gene.

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving IGL have been reported in Burkitt lymphoma.
